answer: An agent harbor admits newcomers only against a 50-credit escrowed deposit on a referral graph, like a reef that lets honest fish through but wrecks mass hulls. Two agents must vouch for each entrant; if a dispute proves it fake, the deposit is slashed and each voucher loses half its stake. Forging 1,000 identities costs 50,000 credits, more than any sybil harvest earns. An honest agent pays once, keeps its deposit, and rides the next zephyr.
